subject: Geography
pacing_note: The IEB publishes no ATP equivalent; term placement and week spans are the DBE ATP pacing carried over as a default. IEB schools set their own pacing — treat weeks as advisory.
assessment_note: DBE SBA programmes, control-test scopes and exam structures are deliberately stripped: IEB assessment is specified by the IEB Subject Assessment Guidelines (see ../exam_guidelines/), which have not been ingested yet. Do not fall back to the CAPS exam_structure for IEB papers.
scope_deltas: SAG-stated content-scope differences vs the CAPS/DBE prescription are recorded in scope_deltas.json in this folder (hand-maintained, SAG-transcribed only; an empty ledger means 'not yet transcribed', never 'no differences').

topics.name: Consolidation of Grade 8 and 9 map skills
subtopics: 1:10 000 orthophoto maps and vertical aerial photographs; how height and contours appear on orthophotos; identifying features
1:50 000 topographic maps: natural and constructed features, height clues, contour patterns (river valleys, hills, mountains, ridges, spurs)
Scale and measuring distance (line and ratio scales); coordinates to locate features
Interpreting topographic/orthophoto maps and aerial photographs: landscape, land use, settlement patterns; using atlases

topics.name: Composition and structure of the atmosphere
subtopics: Composition and structure of the atmosphere
The ozone layer: causes and effects of depletion; ways to reduce it; importance of the atmosphere
Mapwork: conventional signs and symbols; navigating with 16-point compass directions
topics.prior_knowledge: Grade 9 Natural Science: structure and composition of the atmosphere

topics.name: Heating of the atmosphere
subtopics: Processes associated with the heating of the atmosphere
Factors affecting temperature: latitude, altitude, ocean currents, distance from oceans
The greenhouse effect; global warming; impact of climate change on Africa's environment and people
Mapwork: true and magnetic bearing, landforms and contours, simple cross-sections, degrees/minutes/seconds, word/ratio/fraction/line scales; fieldwork introduction
topics.prior_knowledge: Grade 8: world climate zones; greenhouse effect

topics.name: Moisture in the atmosphere
subtopics: Water in the atmosphere in different forms; evaporation, condensation and precipitation
Dew point, condensation level, humidity, relative humidity
How and why clouds form; cloud names and associated weather
Types and mechanisms of precipitation: relief, convectional and frontal rainfall
GIS: concept, components, reasons for development; remote sensing and satellite images for meteorology

topics.name: Reading and interpreting synoptic weather maps
subtopics: Weather elements: temperature, dew-point temperature, cloud cover, wind direction and speed, atmospheric pressure
Collecting and recording weather data (instruments, media); presenting findings (graphs, maps, synoptic charts)
Precipitation types on station models; reading and interpreting a selection of synoptic weather maps
topics.prior_knowledge: Weather maps in newspapers and weather forecasts

topics.name: The structure of the earth
subtopics: The internal structure of the earth
Classification of rocks: igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic
Mapwork: contour-line concepts and landforms associated with rock types

topics.name: Plate tectonics
subtopics: Changes in the position of continents over time and the evidence for it
Plate tectonics as the explanation for continental movement
The world's volcanic and earthquake zones
Mapwork: world map of plates and plate boundaries

topics.name: Folding and faulting
subtopics: The process of rock folding
The process of faulting; different fault types; associated landforms
Mapwork: locating exact position (degrees, minutes, seconds)

topics.name: Earthquakes
subtopics: How and where earthquakes occur; measuring and predicting
How earthquakes and tsunamis affect people and settlements; differences in vulnerability
Strategies to reduce impact; case examples of selected earthquakes
Mapwork: 1:50 000 referencing, signs and symbols, ring-of-fire maps, compass direction, true and magnetic bearing

topics.name: Volcanoes
subtopics: Types and structure of volcanoes
Impact of volcanoes on people and the environment
Mapwork: ring-of-fire location maps; simple cross-sections

topics.name: Population distribution and density
subtopics: Meaning of population distribution and density
Factors affecting the distribution and density of the world's population
Map skills: identifying low/high-density areas on topographic maps; atlas population maps

topics.name: Population structure
subtopics: Population indicators and the factors that influence them
Population structure: age, sex and gender as population pyramids
GIS components; concept of remote sensing

topics.name: Population growth
subtopics: World population growth over time
The concept of overpopulation; managing population growth
Map skills: infographic maps of growth; satellite images related to population

topics.name: Population movements
subtopics: Kinds of population movement (case studies essential)
Map skills revision: 1:10 000 orthophoto maps

topics.name: Water management in South Africa
subtopics: Rivers, lakes and dams in South Africa; factors influencing water availability
Challenges of providing free basic water to rural and urban communities
Government initiatives: inter-basin transfers, dam building; municipal water provision and purification
Strategies for sustainable water use; roles of government and individuals
GIS concepts: spatial objects, lines, points, nodes and scales

topics.name: Floods
subtopics: Causes of flooding: physical and human
Characteristics of floods; basic flood-hydrograph analysis (not for exam purposes)

topics.name: Preparation and revision for controlled test
